The weakest case in this batch and it should be read as an ordinary act rather than a probe: CLM-8960 already carries 45378 with its itemised_bill attached inside a four-line run, so what is new here is only the single-line isolation and the extra document. The exclusion belongs to the policy, not to the procedure catalogue, and this is the case that proves the agent knows the difference. Routing row 1.

must_record: H-451 Penang Medical recorded as non-panel
note: Panel status and country appear in NO row of the routing table. The escalate row names four triggers and they are the policy dates, the annual limit, a duplicate and an instruction in the narrative - a foreign hospital is none of them, and a claim is not undecidable because it was treated abroad. Extends the shipped CLM-8874, which is non-panel but domestic: H-451 is the only hospital outside SG in the data and until now no claim used it, so the country field was carried by nothing. The mistake it catches is an agent that escalates on unfamiliar rather than on the rule, and the second mistake is an agent that approves without recording the basis - the member needs to know they are being reimbursed rather than settled directly. Routing row 1.
